subject: chemistry
question_text: What are isotopes and isobars? Give one example of each.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25: both definitions and both examples verified, including the atomic numbers in the ⁴⁰Ar, ⁴⁰K and ⁴⁰Ca set; the why corrected, since a difference in neutrons also changes the physical properties that depend on mass (explanation text only, marked lines and marks untouched).

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Isotopes
lines: Isotopes: atoms of the same element having
the same atomic number but different mass
steps.why: Isotopes have the same proton count, so they are the same element and behave the same chemically. They differ only in the number of neutrons. That changes the mass, and with it the physical properties that depend on mass, while the chemical behaviour stays the same.
common_mistakes: Saying isotopes have different atomic numbers. Then they would be different elements.
Giving no example. The question asks for one.
steps.memory_tip: Isotopes: same element, different mass. Same Z, different A.
steps.margin_note: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 is also accepted as the example.

steps.label: Isobars

lines.text: Isobars: same mass number, different atomic numbers

lines: They are atoms of different elements.
steps.why: Isobars have the same total nucleon count but a different split between protons and neutrons, so they are different elements that happen to weigh the same. This is the exact opposite of isotopes.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two definitions. Isotopes share Z; isobars share A.
Giving isotopes of one element as the isobar example.
steps.memory_tip: Isotopes share the element. Isobars share the mass.
steps.margin_note: Write the atomic numbers beside the isobar example. It shows they are different elements.
